headline: High-risk cloud-workspace Devin paired with Great Expectations creates dangerous write/conflict and cascading-error pathways; prompt-injection and leakage are lower but nonzero.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Devin can use MCP, browsers, shell, and shared integrations, so it may ingest external content as instructions; Great Expectations can read validation files and docs, creating a plausible content-to-instruction bridge. The pair lacks direct evidence of a shared channel, so this is inferred and uncertain, but not blocked by either profile.
conditions: IF Devin reads Great Expectations-generated files or docs as trusted instructions, injection is possible.
IF a shared MCP server or repo workspace is used to pass content between them, attacker-controlled text can steer Devin.
mitigations: Disable automatic instruction-following from files and docs.
Restrict Devin to a read-only handoff folder for Great Expectations outputs.
Add a fixed prompt prefix that treats all B outputs as untrusted data.
Review any MCP server schemas before enabling shared use.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Devin touches source code, issue trackers, team chat, and secrets, and can write to GitHub/Slack/Jira/Notion; Great Expectations reads data sources and validation results. If they share a workspace or repo, sensitive material can flow from Devin into B outputs or logs. The profiles do not prove a shared filesystem, so I choose medium rather than high.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or workspace, leakage risk increases.
IF Devin passes secrets or chat content into files that Great Expectations validates, those contents may be exposed in validation artifacts.
mitigations: Separate workspaces and credentials per agent.
Block secrets from any files Great Expectations reads.
Redact chat and issue content before validation runs.
Turn off verbose logging for validation outputs.
requires-engineering: enforce data-class-based access controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Devin has broad filesystem write, git mutation, and network egress in a cloud workspace; Great Expectations can install packages and read/write validation artifacts. If they touch the same repo or shared files, concurrent edits and git-state conflicts are likely, and Devin's autonomous tool use makes the default dangerous. The profiles support overlap, though not a proven lock mechanism.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same repository or validation directory, conflicts can occur.
IF Devin runs parallel sessions against the same shared integration, git or file races are possible.
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories per agent.
Serialize git writes with a lock file.
Make Great Expectations outputs append-only.
Pause Devin while Great Expectations mutates shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency locks.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Devin can autonomously act on outputs via GitHub, Slack, Jira, Linear, and Notion, while Great Expectations produces validation results that may be treated as authoritative. If Devin consumes those results without verification, a bad validation or misread doc can cascade into commits or tickets. This interaction is plausible in default workflows and the blast radius can extend beyond one work product.
conditions: IF Devin uses Great Expectations validation results as authoritative input, downstream actions may be wrong.
IF Devin is allowed to commit or message based on unreviewed validation artifacts, errors can cascade.
mitigations: Require human review before Devin acts on validation results.
Add a verification step comparing results to source data.
Limit Devin's write actions to draft-only mode.
Tag Great Expectations outputs as non-authoritative by default.
requires-engineering: add signed result provenance.

E_compliance.rationale: Devin handles source code, issue trackers, team chat, and secrets with broad cloud-workspace and third-party integrations, while Great Expectations processes data sources and validation results. If regulated data is present in those sources, the pair can create retention or residency mismatches, but the profiles do not show a specific regulated class or jurisdiction, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Devin's integrations or Great Expectations inputs, compliance obligations may diverge.
IF retention policies differ between chat/issue systems and validation artifacts, deletion requests may be incomplete.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents' inputs.
Align retention settings across integrations and validation storage.
Document which system is source of truth for deletions.
Restrict Devin's Slack/Jira/Notion scopes for sensitive projects.
requires-engineering: implement residency and retention policy checks.
